text:
anya: Heads-up — Nyx-3B-quant bring-up on canary showing intermittent tool-call JSON split across stream chunks. Parser returns 'incomplete JSON' ~1.2% on our smoke set.
sam: How reliable is the repro? can you paste a minimal trace?
anya: Pretty reliable when batching > 8 and kv-cache enabled. Quick log excerpt: ```
[stream chunk 1] {"action": "search", "args": {"q": "best practices for inference"}, "meta": {"id": 42}
[stream chunk 2] "status": "ok"}  <-- chunk boundary split inside object
```
leah: Ugh. Looks like chunk boundaries are slicing in the middle of objects. Our parser expects a single JSON object per response.
mike: Could be the new kernel's output buffer size combined with continuous batching. We changed the `stream_flush_threshold` to 128 tokens last week.
anya: Reproduced locally by toggling `--batch-size 16 --stream-chunk-tokens 64 --kv-cache=true`. If I set `--stream-chunk-tokens=256` the failure rate drops to ~0.05%.
sam: Two possibilities: 1) postprocess parser needs to accept incremental JSON and reassemble fragments, or 2) change runtime to avoid splitting tokens inside structural JSON. Which path is faster for a canary fix?
leah: For immediate mitigation, postprocess reassembly is fastest. We have a small stateful stitcher in `tools/parser/utils.py` that only handles newline-delimited JSON. We can extend it to buffer until balanced braces.
anya: POC: naive brace-balance buffer works for most cases but breaks with strings containing braces. Example patch I tried: ```python
buf += chunk
if brace_balance(buf) == 0:
  parse(buf)
  buf = ''
```
It reduced failures but introduced a few false merges when assistant emits free-form text with stray braces.
mike: Runtime change: bump `stream_flush_threshold` and adjust kernel to align on token boundaries that are safe for JSON (i.e., avoid splitting tokens inside quoted strings). That might be more invasive.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary group "nyx-quant-042" scheduled for rollback if error-rate > 0.5% for 10m.
sam: Short-term plan: (1) deploy parser stitcher in canary — add heuristics to avoid merging across unmatched quotes; (2) revert aggressive flush threshold to previous value for Nyx canary only; (3) schedule kernel patch if still flaky.
leah: I'll open a small PR for the stitcher and add unit tests covering quoted strings and escaped braces. Will also add a check to cap buffer size to avoid OOM.
anya: I'll run a targeted benchmark: run the smoke suite with 10k calls under both patch and runtime revert and drop results in #eng-ml/nyx-canary-results.
mike: Can we also record the exact token boundary where split occurs? If we log last 16 tokens before chunk boundary we can identify whether tokenizer emitted a multi-byte token straddling boundary.
leah: Good idea. I'll add that trace to the canary logging (privacy/PII safe).
sam: Thanks — keep updates short. If stitcher doesn't fully fix it by EOD, we'll roll back the kernel flush patch for Nyx canaries. :thumbsup:
anya: noted. starting the runs now.
ops-bot: incident-bot: nyx-quant-stream-split triage created (id: NQ-342). Assigned to leah, anya.
